title: Memory–sample tradeoffs for noisy parity learning
formal: Do there exist absolute constants \(c_{1},c_{2}>0\) and \(n_{0}\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge n_{0}\), every \(0<\varepsilon <1/2\) and every one-pass learner recovering a uniformly random \(x\in \{0,1\}^{n}\) with probability at least \(2/3\) from the noisy parity samples defined below, its worst-case memory S and maximum sample count T satisfy \(S\ge c_{1}n^{2}/\varepsilon ^{2}\) or \(T\ge 2^{c_{2}n}\)? Constants are independent of \(n, \varepsilon\) and the learner, and \(\varepsilon\) may tend to zero with n. This states the bounded-error recovery interpretation of Conjecture 1; it does not additionally require a lower bound at exponentially small success probability.
context:
Without noise, every observation is a correct linear relation about the hidden vector. Here the relation is only slightly more likely to be right than wrong when \(\varepsilon\) is small. The question asks whether this forces a quadratic loss in the storage threshold as the bias tends to zero.

The source proves that a learner needs \(\Omega (n^{2}/\varepsilon )\) memory or exponentially many samples, and records an upper bound using \(O(n^{2}/\varepsilon ^{2})\) memory and \(O(n/\varepsilon ^{2})\) samples. The conjecture asks whether the stronger memory dependence is necessary below an exponential sample budget.

The lower bound concerns retained information, not the time needed to process it. It must hold for arbitrary state-transition rules and therefore would be unconditional even though efficient learning of noisy parity is also used as a computational hardness assumption.

For \(\varepsilon\) fixed away from zero, the two memory bounds differ only by constants. The unresolved content is their uniform dependence on \(\varepsilon\), together with an exponential sample threshold whose exponent does not shrink with \(\varepsilon\).

The 2024 DIMACS project abstract identifies the same \(n^{2}/\varepsilon ^{2}\)-versus-exponential tradeoff as its long-term goal and describes intermediate observations in a modified model. It is evidence of continued study, not a proved lower bound or a fresh claim that all later work has been exhausted.
why: Would quantify how observation noise increases the storage needed for a central learning problem, strengthening unconditional limits relevant to streaming learning and bounded-storage cryptography.

references.title: Memory-Sample Lower Bounds for Learning Parity with Noise
references.authors: Garg, Sumegha; Kothari, Pravesh K.; Liu, Pengda; Raz, Ran

definitions: Arithmetic in 𝔽\(_{2}=\{0,1\}\) uses addition and multiplication modulo two; \(\langle a,x\rangle =\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}x_{i}\) mod 2. First choose x uniformly from \(\{0,1\}^{n}\) and hold it fixed. Independently for each t, choose \(a_{t}\) uniformly from \(\{0,1\}^{n}\) and a noise bit \(Z_{t}\) with \(\Pr [Z_{t}=1]=1/2- \varepsilon\); observe \((a_{t},b_{t})\) with \(b_{t}=\langle a_{t},x\rangle +Z_{t}\) mod 2. Noise bits, query vectors and internal learner coins are mutually independent. The learner outputs one estimate x̂; success means \(\hat\{x\}=x\), and its probability averages over x, all observations and internal coins. The learner sees each sample once in order, cannot choose \(a_{t}\) or revisit discarded observations, and has no computational-time restriction. Formally use a branching program with \(T+1\) layers and width at most \(2^{S}\), one start vertex and one outgoing edge for each possible sample at each nonterminal vertex, all going to the next layer. Leaves, possibly in earlier layers, are labelled by estimates in \(\{0,1\}^{n}\). Randomized learners may use fresh coins to choose state updates; retained coins are part of the state. Equivalently, the lower bound may be checked on deterministic nonuniform programs, since a random tape can be fixed to achieve at least the average success under this fixed input distribution without increasing width or length. The program may depend on n and \(\varepsilon\); its transition description, current layer and input sample are not charged as stored data. Memory counts persistent state bits, \(S=\lceil \log _{2}(\operatorname{width})\rceil\), and T is the maximum number of consumed samples, not its expectation. No hypothesis is made about the hardness of LPN in unrestricted computation.
answer_criterion: Prove the universal bounded-error memory/sample tradeoff with constants uniform in \(\varepsilon\), or refute that asymptotic claim by showing that no such constants can work. A bound \(\Omega (n^{2}/\varepsilon ), a\) result only for constant \(\varepsilon\), or a lower bound in a restricted statistical-query model does not settle the proposed dependence on noise.
